reviews.text:
I adopted three small animals from this store.

I took them to the vet immediately after adopting them, but all of them were ill, and their illnesses were quite advanced. They all died within six months of adoption.

It's truly appalling; it seems they don't allow any adjustment period after the animals arrive at the store, or they're just being fed without proper care.

I called the store to confirm their birth dates and informed them of their deaths, but all I got was a dismissive "Oh, really?"

That was a truly hurtful response.

I hope they not only improve the environment but also provide proper basic training for their staff.

I will never come back.

I would like to give it 0 stars if possible.

The birds were in poor condition.

I expressed my concerns to the staff, but their attitude was cold. I doubt they value customer feedback.

That bird was so pitiful.

You shouldn't get small animals from here.

The living conditions of these animals are absolutely unacceptable.

I was truly shocked and furious to see the living conditions of the animals in this shop.

I have visited this shop four times. And each time, I witnessed situations that made me wonder, "How can they keep animals in such conditions?"

What I want to emphasize here is that this is not just a problem with one animal. From what I have seen, there are significant problems with the overall living conditions of the animals.

No matter how many times I visited, I noticed dirty cages, dirty water, dirty bedding and hiding places, and cages that were far too small for the size of the animals.

Some blankets and hiding places were clearly soiled with feces and urine. The water containers were also so dirty that it seemed they were not properly cleaned.

Furthermore, during my four visits, I repeatedly saw that there was no visible food in the cages of multiple animals.

This wasn't just a one-time occurrence.

I visited four times, and I saw similar conditions each time.

I was particularly concerned about a small brown animal with large eyes and a long tail. It's clearly a nocturnal animal, extremely sensitive to light.

The animal was barely moving in its very small cage, constantly hiding in or under a dirty blanket, seemingly to escape the bright lights of the store.

I saw this animal four times.

And all four times, it was almost completely still, just lying there.

Of course, it was breathing, but it was barely moving.

It's not easy to simply dismiss it as "just sleeping."

If you see a nocturnal, light-sensitive animal hiding under a blanket in a brightly lit store, wouldn't it be natural to question whether its natural rhythm and necessary environment are being properly considered?

And I thought the monkeys' living conditions were truly terrible.

The cages were far too small, with insufficient space for movement.

And the monkeys were repeating the same movements for hours in those cramped cages.

They were jumping from one end of the cage to the other, doing somersaults repeatedly, and going back and forth in the same spot over and over again.

Over and over.

It was like this for a long time.

Of course, it's normal for animals to play and move around energetically.

But the monkeys I saw here seemed to have almost nothing else to do in their cramped cages, and they appeared to be endlessly repeating the same movements.

They are animals that normally climb, jump, explore their surroundings, and engage in a variety of behaviors.

Yet, they were repeating the same movements over and over in cages that were too small.

Seeing that made me truly distressed.

Furthermore, there were bats in cages in the store.

Bats.

Nocturnal wild animals.

And they were placed in a brightly lit store.

I really wonder, "Why?"

Why is it necessary to keep such animals in such an environment?

And I didn't get a good impression of the birds and other exotic animals either.

Crowded cages, dirty environments, conditions that seemed to prevent them from moving around or hiding properly.

This isn't just a problem with one cage.

I've visited four times, and each time I've had concerns about the animals' living conditions.

I truly cannot understand exhibiting and selling exotic wild animals in such conditions.

Animals are not commodities.

They are not store decorations.

They are not "cute exhibits" to show to customers.

And they are not something that can be kept in small cages to save space.

Animals need sufficient space.

They need clean water.

They need appropriate food.

They need a hygienic environment.

They need a safe place to rest.

And above all, they need an environment that suits their natural habits and lifestyle.

This is especially true when dealing with exotic animals; I believe it's a given.

What angers me the most is that customers only see the animals for about five minutes, think they're "cute," and leave, without knowing how the animals spend their day.

Customers can't see it.

Monkeys repeating the same movements for hours in cramped cages.

Nocturnal animals hiding in dirty blankets to escape the light in a brightly lit store.

The water is dirty.

The hiding places are soiled with feces and urine.

That's why I don't want to turn a blind eye.

This isn't just a one-time occurrence.

I've seen it with my own eyes four times.

That's why I want someone to properly investigate this issue.

Don't just look at one animal; look at all the animals there.

Check the size of the cages.

Check the water.

Check the food.

Check the hygiene of their bedding and hiding places.

And actually observe how the animals behave over long periods of time.

Animals repeating the same movements for hours in cages that are too small.

Nocturnal animals constantly fleeing from bright lights.

The water and cages are visibly dirty.

When I actually see these conditions, I personally cannot possibly think, "This is okay."

I believe these animals have the right to live in a better environment. Please, someone, actually check on the condition of these animals.

And please, don't turn a blind eye.

Having personally witnessed this four times, I absolutely cannot recommend this shop.

To me, this is not responsible animal care.

Even when I called out "Excuse me," there was no response. When I asked to see the turtles, they silently handed me an open tank and disappeared without any explanation. I've been to many pet shops, but I've never seen staff like that before.

I don't think I'll ever go back.

I don't know if it's the same person mentioned in other comments, but I strongly recommend asking to be served by a staff member other than the woman with the bright hair.

There are many animals, but without exception, they are all poorly cared for, very poorly, extremely poorly. Please do not buy anything from this store. If you don't have the resources and space to properly care for them, don't keep so many exotic creatures to attract attention. I have never seen a zoo that takes such poor care of its animals. And on the second floor, there's a creature that looks like a pangolin priced at 800,000? Isn't that illegal?

It breaks my heart to see squirrel monkeys being kept in unbelievably small cages...

If they can only be kept in such conditions, I wish they wouldn't sell them. 💔
There were some rare small animals, and it was fun just looking at them!

Animal cruelty is apparently legal and supported in Tokyo, as seen with this horror house of a "pet store". I'm not the first to comment on that and I hope I won't be the last. This place should be closed down and its animals should get taken care of by people with an actual heart who could give them a better life than the one they have in this terrible place where even the cages are way too small.
It's interesting to see all the different kinds of pets.

Apparently, because fennec foxes cost 1.2 million yen, they're kept in small cages for six years.

Owls are also kept chained for 15 years.
Good.
This is the place to go if you want to get a pet cheaply! However, I've bought two rabbits in the past, and both of them got sick.

The adult Java sparrow I adopted from this shop was incredibly tame and friendly.

At the shop, it was chirping sadly by itself, but when I approached it, it started singing, and I fell in love at first sight!

The shop told me it wasn't hand-tamed, but
by the second day, it was completely attached to me and even allowed me to hold it.

It's even communicating with other Java sparrows, chirping away.

It was a bit pricey, but I'm so glad I was able to adopt such a healthy and energetic bird.

ANIMAL CRUELTY IN ITS MOST HORRIFIC EXPRESSION, endangered monkeys, reptiles and birds in the smallest cages, its as sad and horrificas you walk through the space  I’ve never seen anything like it in a “pet shop” .

This old-fashioned pet shop, operating long before Shin-Okubo became a Korean food district, evokes the good old days of the Showa era.

The shop has a large, resident dog that always seems to be sleeping peacefully, which is quite memorable. I remember it being featured on television in the past, and it makes you wonder, "How many generations of dogs are they now?" It gives you a sense of history.

Furthermore, on the second floor, there's a free-to-enter "mini zoo" area. Free-roaming gamecocks are there, which can be a bit of a surprise if you go without knowing what to expect (laughs).
I love it because you can interact with the animals more than at a real zoo!
It wasn't exactly clean, but they had a variety of animals on display, and I used it several times. The staff were friendly, so I didn't have any particular issues.
The selection was good, the store was clean and the staff were very friendly.

I recently purchased a hamster from your store, but it became ill and passed away a few days after purchase.
It seems that it was in poor health from the time I bought it, which is very sad.

Furthermore, the cage, food, and other products I purchased with it were of poor quality, breaking easily and being difficult to use.

I would never recommend this store to anyone looking to buy a pet.

I strongly recommend trying another store before you regret your decision.
There are a lot of unusual animals. The staff generally seem unmotivated and not many knowledgeable people. The animals I want are often already homed, which is frustrating.

There wasn't much to see, but it is a pet shop you can easily visit while in Japan. It is good for finding supplies.

The Eurasian Eagle Owl on the second floor was magnificent.

I visited exactly 10 years ago, and I wonder if it is the same individual.

There is a Shamo in the chicken coop on the opposite side, and its appearance is far superior to that of the average chickens.

If I could have taken it home, I would have liked to buy one.
The shop where Walther often uses the live stream of Battlefield Tornado
There's a bird called konnichiwa there, a big white dog wandering around inside, various animals, they're clean and well-cared for, it's a wonderful place.

I revisited and was so glad to see Bubu-chan the softshell turtle looking so healthy 😊
The Samoyed resident dog on the first floor is also very gentle ♪
It's a precious urban zoo ◎
───────────── On the second floor of the pet shop, you can experience feeding Bubu-chan the softshell turtle ♪
She was so cute as she gently ate the apples and bananas! 🐢
I was a little scared, but she was calm and reassuring 😊
There are also other rare animals like owls, and you can see them quite close up, making it a valuable experience 👀✨
It has a quiet atmosphere that adults and children alike can enjoy; it's a wonderful hidden spot 👍
I always find myself stopping by whenever I'm passing by ♪

When I went there about five years ago, I was honestly surprised that it wasn't very clean and that expired food was being sold, but when I went back in 2025, I was relieved to see that the store was well-maintained, the animal kennels were well-maintained, and the staff were extremely friendly! I go there to buy bird food, hamster food, and more! There's a wide variety of items, so it's fun!

I heard there are some rare animals on the second floor... Cats and dogs are displayed in the front, and birds and fish are in the back for sale. As it is a pet shop, there is a huge variety of food and other goods available.

This store practices animal cruelty, pure and simple. Most of the exotic animals that are being sold are NOT pets and should not be sold as such, and their living conditions are horrible. The animals live in small, tiny and unclean cages. The monkey was trying to get out of its small enclosure and the birds were losing their feathers from the stress. Just awful to witness. They are living beings and should be treated with the dignity and respect they deserve.

This shop is very appealing to animal lovers.

Bubu-chan is so cute and癒し (healing/soothing)!

ABSOLUTELY HORRIFIC place for all the poor animals to be trapped in. I would rate 0 stars if I could. Birds are put into extremely small and filthy cages (looks like they haven’t been cleaned in weeks). In some of them you were barely able to tell if they were dead or alive. There was even a monkey trapped in a small plastic box. All the animals were showing signs of stress. You would think for the price they are selling these animals I.e. 400k for the parrot and 2.5mil yen for the monkey) they would provide more humane living conditions. There is nothing moral or cute or normal about this place - I wouldn’t even call it a “zoo”. I hope some organizations will finally notice and step in to help these animals. The owner should be ashamed of themselves.

The living conditions in the store are so bad that I feel sorry for the animals. There are cages with tons of droppings on them, and the parakeets and squirrel monkeys are kept in a chaotic environment, which must be stressful for them, and above all, the cages are far too small. The cage for the squirrel monkeys in particular was so small that I wondered if they had just assigned them a spare cage, and it made me question their ethics and everything else.
The inside is a bit dirty, but there are animals you wouldn't normally see in a pet shop, so it's interesting and feels like you've come to a zoo.

I stop by regularly because I want to see Kamon-chan and Dandy-chan.

They're so incredibly cute!

Thanks for letting me pet them again today! 😍
I've been going to this shop for over ten years, ever since Lemon was a puppy, and for the past two years since we moved, I've continued to go there even though it takes me over an hour by train.
This pet shop has been in business in Shin-Okubo for a long time. They also have some rare animals.

I got my leg fur trimmed at ZOO in Shin-Okubo ✂️
At first I was a little nervous and my heart was pounding...but before I knew it, I was surrounded by dogs! I even gave a nose kiss to a fluffy brown dog through the cart, and I had a long staring contest with a fluffy white dog. It was so much fun, I couldn't tell if I was there for grooming or just to socialize with dogs 🐶🐱

The staff gently held me still so I could stay still, and they trimmed my legs neatly. The result is very comfortable, and it's much easier to walk now.

🐾 My recommendations
😸 They carefully trim the fur on your legs
😸 The staff are gentle and supportive
😸 You can say hello to the dogs (a chance to make friends!)

It might be a little nerve-wracking, but it's the perfect place for cats who want to make friends with dogs ✨

Since purchasing my mini lion rabbit, I've been using their pet hotel and nail trimming services.

I'm grateful that I can entrust my rabbit to them with complete peace of mind.

Boycott unscrupulous companies! Locking animals up like prisoners in filthy, cramped spaces is heartbreaking. I thought Japan loved animals so much. You guys are incredibly heartless! And the whole place stinks because you're not taking care of them at all. They're so pitiful, rotting away.
The animals are very pitiful. Please do not go there to encourage purchases.
There are all kinds of pets, from common ones to more unusual ones, and it's really soothing.

We purchased a baby budgie (only about one month old) from this store. Within less than a week — despite being kept in a clean, warm, and caring environment — the bird suddenly became ill and died.

After visiting a vet, we were told the bird was riddled with parasites, which likely developed from poor breeding and crowded conditions before purchase.

This was extremely heartbreaking. We'd bonded with the bird, gave it constant care and attention — including a warm cage, air conditioning, quiet environment, and hand-feeding. My girlfriend has also looked after birds many times before and is experienced in how to look after them.

The bird did not die from neglect, but from internal issues it clearly already had when sold to us.

This shop had the baby birds kept in one cage together. If our bird was infected, it is highly likely the others are too. I certainly hope other customers don’t go through this same painful experience.

I urge the store to improve its animal health checks and take responsibility. Selling such vulnerable animals without proper care is cruel. Please be Be cautious if you’re considering purchasing a pet here. If you also come in person, the conditions are certainly far from ideal for poor animals.

-------

I purchased a budgie chick from this store when it was about one month old.

Despite being carefully raised in a clean and comfortable environment, it suddenly became ill after just a few days and unfortunately passed away.

I took it to the vet, who diagnosed it with numerous parasites.

The vet said that this was most likely due to overcrowding and poor hygiene before selling it.

We raised it with love and care, paying close attention to temperature control and diet. My girlfriend also has extensive experience raising birds and did everything we could for it, including feeding it carefully. However, the bird died in our hands. This was not due to our caregiving error, and we believe it already had internal problems at the time of sale.

When we purchased it, the store had multiple chicks in the same cage, so it is highly likely that the other birds were also infected.

We strongly urge you to thoroughly check the health of animals before selling them so that other customers do not have the same painful experience.
If you are thinking of purchasing, please make your decision carefully.

I bought a fancy rat, but the conditions it's being kept in are horrible. Rats are highly social animals, so unless there's a very good reason, they should generally be kept in groups. However, here, I kept only one rat in a cage, with no bedding and a wire mesh floor. There's no way a rat can grow up healthy in an environment like that. Other rats besides the one I bought were also in the same horrible conditions. It's bordering on abuse. I hope it disappears soon.

I'm happy that I can get a partial cut for my dog ​​starting from 500 yen. 
It's on the first floor, so it's easy to get in, and I'm happy that I can do it without making a reservation.
Cool animals but depressing conditions
A young female employee was just watching the dog eating feces and did nothing. The staff member had light-colored hair and a bad attitude. I would not leave my pet here.
There is a wide variety of small animals.

The first floor has regular pets, but the second floor has unusual creatures.
It's like a zoo, and it's fun just to look around.
It seemed like a shop frequented by celebrities.
I'm always grateful for their service; the staff are always kind and it's a great shop.

There was a dog walking around the store, and it was so cute 😊
The staff were also very kind, it was a really great store! …

It was fun to see unusual animals and reptiles that you wouldn't normally find in a pet shop, and there was even a big dog walking around inside.

I went to buy some hamster supplies, and they had a wide variety, so I was able to buy exactly what I wanted.
cute
I love Shin-Okubo because it's full of delicious food. The Crocs were incredibly tasty. When I put lemon on the octopus, it was so yummy!
There are lots of different animals 👍 …

I fell in love at first sight with the fennec fox I saw at the Roppongi Zoo, and I was so happy to be reunited with it.

It's a price I can't afford, but
I sat next to it and touched its chin like a cat, and it narrowed its eyes.

I love this fennec fox so much,
I hope we can meet again soon,
and I hope it finds a good family soon.
thank you.
It's fun just to go and see the rare animals.
I went to buy reptile food, but I wish they had a few more varieties.

The reptiles all seemed healthy, but everything else was extremely sick and unwell. I have worked in veterinary clinics and can tell when animals are clearly sick, but I think it wouldn’t even take a trained eye to see how unhealthy these poor animals are. Death will honestly be kinder to them than the suffering they must face here.

All of the bunnies were aggressively shaking and can’t keep their heads up. Some of the other rodents have no room to hide. The monkey was hitting itself against the cage that is far too small for such an exotic species. Some of the birds running away when you passed by them. And the worst part of all that I wish I never saw was the 2nd floor. There were two dogs in cages who were clearly moved up there because they are now older and no one wanted to adopt them, so instead of placing them downstairs and improving their chance of adoption or putting them in a more spacious cage for their adult size, they are cramped in a cage that is the equivalent of putting an adult human in a bathtub for the rest of their life. Japan has always had an issue with puppymills and only selling animals that are babies, and then discarding the ones who don’t get a home, but this was the most horrific thing I’d ever seen. The dogs were so traumatized upstairs that you could hear their screams from outside, and they would pace back and forth in such a repeated pattern that even it you came up to them  and got on their level it was like they were stuck in a trance they couldn’t escape or stop. They label the 2nd floor as a “free animal experience” but what it really is, is a place for them to throw all the animals in that no one wants to buy. And it seems no one even knows its up there because it isn’t connected to the main shop on the first floor where all the “cuter” animals are. I hope these animals will at least be bought by people who can give them a 2nd chance.
I bought large crickets here, but the dead ones were also counted and packed into the bag. The price was also higher than other stores. …

Dessert buffet available
Popular with young people
Interesting to see the animals in there, but definitely heartbreaking. They ahad a little monkey in a parrot cage. Dogs and cats isolated in their cages. Rabbits in tiny cages. …

I went there looking for hamsters.
The dogs and cats are okay, but the conditions for the small, exotic, and aquatic animals are terrible. …

There are many rare animals.

It feels more like an indoor zoo than a pet shop, and the children were very …
